q: The Marathwada Rail Coach Factory, which manufactures passenger coaches, is located at:
e: The Marathwada Rail Coach Factory, which manufactures passenger coaches, is located at Latur in Maharashtra.

q: The Train 18 train sets, marketed as Vande Bharat, owe their design and manufacture to:
e: Train 18 train sets, marketed as Vande Bharat, were designed and manufactured by Integral Coach Factory, Chennai.

q: The Modern Coach Factory, a production unit manufacturing passenger coaches, is located at:
e: Modern Coach Factory, a production unit manufacturing passenger coaches, is located at Raebareli, Uttar Pradesh.

q: Electric locomotives are the principal outturn of which of the following production units?
e: Chittaranjan Locomotive Works is the production unit whose principal outturn is electric locomotives.

q: Wheels and axles for rolling stock are the main products of the production unit located at:
e: Rail Wheel Factory at Yelahanka, Bengaluru, mainly produces wheels and axles for rolling stock.

q: When it was originally set up, the Rail Wheel Factory at Yelahanka was known as the:
e: Rail Wheel Factory at Yelahanka was originally set up under the name Wheel and Axle Plant.

q: Before it received its present name, the Diesel Loco Modernisation Works at Patiala was set up under the name:
e: Diesel Loco Modernisation Works at Patiala was set up under its former name, Diesel Component Works.

q: Heavy-duty diesel breakdown cranes are a well-known manufacture of the workshop at:
e: Jamalpur workshop is well known for manufacture of heavy-duty diesel breakdown cranes, besides its other repair and manufacturing work.

q: Periodic Overhaul of passenger coaches and EMU stock is the main line of work of the Central Railway workshop at:
e: Matunga workshop of Central Railway at Mumbai has Periodic Overhaul of passenger coaches and EMU stock as its main line of work.

q: Southern Railway's Carriage Works and Loco Works are both located at:
e: Southern Railway's Carriage Works and Loco Works are both located at Perambur, Chennai.

q: The full form of the abbreviation COFMOW, the organisation set up for the modernisation of workshops, is:

options.A: Central Office for Manufacture of Wagons
options.C: Central Organisation for Modernisation of Workshops
options.D: Central Organisation for Maintenance of Workshops

e: COFMOW stands for Central Organisation for Modernisation of Workshops, set up for modernisation of railway workshops.

q: Passenger coaches of the 'LHB' design are so called because the design and technology for them came from:

options.A: A British coach-building firm of London
options.C: The first Indian engineer who designed the coach

e: LHB coaches take their name from Linke-Hofmann-Busch, the German firm from which the coach design and technology came.

q: Stainless steel is the material used for the body shells of passenger coaches of which of the following designs?
e: LHB design coach body shells are made of stainless steel, unlike the conventional ICF design shells.

q: Merit rating of workshop staff differs from job evaluation in that merit rating is an assessment of:

options.B: The machine on which the work is done
options.C: The method of doing the work
options.D: The worker, that is, his efficiency, conduct and performance

e: Merit rating assesses the worker himself - his efficiency, conduct and performance - whereas job evaluation assesses the job and its requirements.

q: In workshop costing terminology, 'defectives' are distinguished from 'spoilage' in that:

options.A: Defectives can never be rectified, whereas spoilage can always be rectified
options.B: Defectives are sold at full price, whereas spoilage is sold at a discount
options.C: Defectives can be rectified and brought up to the required standard by incurring additional expenditure, whereas spoilage cannot be rectified economically and has to be rejected or sold as scrap
options.D: There is no difference between the two terms

e: Defectives can be rectified to the required standard by extra expenditure, while spoilage cannot be rectified economically and is rejected or sold as scrap.

q: Boilers, tanks and other plate and pressure-vessel work, both fabrication and repair, is the speciality of which shop of a railway workshop?
e: The boiler shop specialises in boilers, tanks and other plate and pressure-vessel work, both fabrication and repair.

q: Machined components are fitted together and built up into sub-assemblies and complete units in which shop of a workshop?
e: In the fitting shop, machined components are fitted together and built up into sub-assemblies and complete units.

q: Which maintenance concept enlists the operators themselves in the routine care and upkeep of the equipment they operate, with zero breakdowns and zero defects as its aim?
e: Total Productive Maintenance enlists operators themselves in routine care of their equipment, aiming at zero breakdowns and zero defects.

q: Machines and equipment are arranged in a workshop under a good plant layout principally so that:

options.A: The number of machines installed in the shop is increased
options.B: The number of workers required in the shop is reduced
options.C: Material handling is minimised and a smooth flow of work is ensured
options.D: The appearance of the shop floor is improved

e: A good plant layout arranges machines and equipment to minimise material handling and ensure a smooth flow of work through the shop.

q: However fast the other operations of a production line in a workshop may be, the effective output of the line as a whole cannot exceed the capacity of its:

options.B: Bottleneck operation, that is, the operation with the least capacity

e: Line output is limited by its bottleneck operation, the operation with the least capacity; faster operations cannot raise output beyond that rate.

q: A heated steel component is cooled very slowly, generally in the furnace itself, so that the steel becomes softer and more ductile. This heat treatment is known as:
e: Annealing is slow cooling, generally in the furnace itself, which makes steel softer and more ductile; quenching hardens by rapid cooling.

q: A steel component is hardened only in its outer surface, its core being left comparatively soft and tough. This process is known as:
e: Case hardening hardens only the outer surface of a steel component, leaving the core comparatively soft and tough.

q: Zinc is the metal with which iron or steel articles are coated in the process known as:
e: Galvanising coats iron or steel articles with zinc to protect them against corrosion; tinning uses tin and chromium plating uses chromium.

q: Acetylene burnt in oxygen produces the welding flame used in:
e: Burning acetylene in oxygen gives the flame used in oxy-acetylene or gas welding.

q: Flat surfaces are produced by means of a reciprocating single-point cutting tool moving over a stationary workpiece on a:
e: A shaping machine produces flat surfaces with a reciprocating single-point cutting tool moving over a stationary workpiece.

q: Very close dimensional tolerances and a fine surface finish are obtained on a machined component, by the action of an abrasive wheel, in the operation of:

options.C: Joining of two pieces of metal

e: Grinding with an abrasive wheel removes very little metal to obtain close dimensional tolerances and a fine surface finish.

q: Any component made within the specified limits of size will fit and function in any corresponding assembly without further fitting. Manufacture of this kind is called:
e: Interchangeable manufacture means components made within specified limits fit and function in any corresponding assembly without further fitting.

q: Cavities formed in a casting by gases and moisture entrapped in the mould during pouring of the molten metal are known as:
e: Blow holes are cavities in a casting caused by gases and moisture entrapped in the mould during pouring of molten metal.

q: A tight shrink fit of a new steel tyre on a wheel centre is obtained in the wheel shop by:

options.A: Heating the tyre so that it expands, placing it over the wheel centre and allowing it to cool and contract
options.B: Pressing the cold tyre over the wheel centre by hydraulic pressure alone
options.C: Welding the tyre to the wheel centre all round
options.D: Bolting the tyre to the wheel centre

e: A steel tyre is heated to expand, placed over the wheel centre and allowed to cool and contract, giving a tight shrink fit.

q: Flat and profiled surfaces are produced by a rotating multi-point cutter on a machine known as the:
e: A milling machine produces flat and profiled surfaces with a rotating multi-point cutter.

q: A stationary cutting tool with the workpiece reciprocating past it is the working arrangement of which of the following machines?
e: In a planing machine the cutting tool is stationary and the workpiece reciprocates past it, the reverse arrangement of a shaping machine.

q: Enlarging and finishing a hole that has already been drilled is the machining operation called:
e: Boring is enlarging and finishing a hole already drilled, giving it accurate size and finish.

q: Whether the dimensions of a component lie within the prescribed tolerance limits can be checked quickly, without measuring the exact dimension, by using:
e: Limit gauges, GO and NO-GO, quickly check whether a dimension lies within prescribed tolerance without measuring its exact value.

q: Fresh workers are recruited and trained in a workshop in place of those who have left. In cost accounting, this recruitment and training expenditure is treated as:

options.A: A direct labour cost of jobs
options.B: A direct material cost of jobs
options.D: Overhead (on-cost), as it cannot be charged to any particular job

e: Recruitment and training cost of fresh workers cannot be charged to any particular job, so it is treated as overhead or on-cost.

q: A Basic Training Centre attached to a workshop trains apprentices and staff. In workshop costing, the cost of running such a centre is borne as:

options.A: A direct charge on manufacture jobs

e: The cost of running a Basic Training Centre attached to a workshop is borne as general on-cost of the workshop.

q: The quantity of work which a qualified worker can turn out in one hour working at standard performance is denoted by the term:
e: A standard hour is the quantity of work a qualified worker can turn out in one hour at standard performance, used as a measure of work content.

q: Unit costs of different workshops become comparable with each other mainly when all the workshops adopt:

options.D: A common system of labour pay sheets

e: Unit costs of different workshops become comparable mainly when all adopt uniform costing principles and methods.

q: Programmed outturn is compared with actual outturn, through bar/Gantt charts, by which organisation of a workshop?
e: The Production Control Organisation compares programmed outturn with actual outturn, using bar or Gantt charts, to control workshop production.

q:
Consider the following statements about the debits raised under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense:
1. Labour charges reach Workshop Manufacturing Suspense through the labour pay sheets.
2. On-cost reaches Workshop Manufacturing Suspense through apportionment of the on-cost collected for the period.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: labour reaches Workshop Manufacturing Suspense through labour pay sheets, and on-cost reaches it through apportionment of on-cost collected for the period.

q: The work completed and transferred out of a workshop during a period, expressed in quantity or value, is known in workshop parlance as its:
e: Outturn is the work completed and transferred out of a workshop during a period, expressed in quantity or value.

q: In the costing records of a workshop, the step by which a shop's collected on-cost is finally charged out to the individual jobs executed in that shop is termed:
e: Absorption is the final charging of a shop's collected on-cost to individual jobs; allocation is direct assignment and apportionment is sharing on a basis.

q: A workshop distinguishes 'time keeping' from 'time booking'. 'Time keeping' in this distinction means:

options.A: Recording the attendance of workers, i.e., their time of arrival at and departure from the workshop
options.B: Recording the time spent by a worker on each job
options.C: Fixing the allowed time for a job
options.D: Preparing the labour pay sheets of the shop

e: Time keeping records attendance, i.e. arrival and departure of workers, while time booking records time spent by a worker on each job.

q: Under Emerson's efficiency bonus plan followed for workshop wage payment, a worker earns his bonus:

options.A: At a flat 50 per cent of the value of the time saved, at every level of saving
options.B: On a graduated scale related to his efficiency, the bonus beginning at a prescribed minimum level of efficiency, commonly 66-2/3 per cent
options.C: Only when his efficiency exceeds 100 per cent of the standard
options.D: In the form of two different piece rates, according as he attains the standard output or not

e: Under Emerson's efficiency bonus plan, bonus is on a graduated scale linked to efficiency and begins at a prescribed minimum, commonly 66-2/3 per cent efficiency.

q: Under Merrick's multiple piece-rate system, a worker whose efficiency rises above 100 per cent of the standard is paid at:

options.B: 110 per cent of the ordinary piece rate
options.C: 150 per cent of the ordinary piece rate
options.D: 120 per cent of the ordinary piece rate

e: Under Merrick's multiple piece-rate system, efficiency above 100 per cent is paid at 120 per cent of the ordinary piece rate, the highest of the graduated rates.

q: The relaxation (fatigue) allowance built into the allowed time for a workshop job is characterised by the fact that it:

options.A: Varies with the nature of the work and the working conditions, such as posture, heat and the weights handled
options.B: Is a uniform percentage for all jobs in all shops
options.C: Is payable in cash along with the wages of the worker
options.D: Is fixed by the Workshop Accounts Office

e: Relaxation or fatigue allowance in allowed time varies with the nature of work and conditions such as posture, heat and weights handled; it is not a uniform percentage.

q: Limestone is added as flux to the charge fed into a foundry cupola in a workshop in order to:

options.A: Serve as the main fuel for melting the metal in the cupola
options.B: Combine with the impurities and ash in the charge and form slag, which can be removed from the molten metal
options.C: Cool the molten metal quickly before it is poured
options.D: Increase the weight of the castings produced from the melt

e: Limestone flux in a cupola combines with impurities and ash in the charge to form slag, which is removed from the molten metal; coke is the fuel.

q: While computing the machine-hour rate of a machine in a workshop, which of the following is treated as a standing (fixed) charge of the machine?

options.A: Power consumed by the machine while it is working
options.B: Coolants and lubricants consumed by the machine
options.C: Rent for the floor space occupied by the machine
options.D: Consumable tools used on the machine

e: Rent for floor space occupied by a machine is a standing or fixed charge in the machine-hour rate, while power and consumables vary with working.

q: When the officers of a workshop speak of the 'outturn' of the workshop for a month, they refer to:

options.A: The total wages paid in the workshop during the month
options.B: The number of workers on the rolls of the workshop
options.C: The balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense at the end of the month
options.D: The work completed and transferred out of the workshop during the period, expressed in quantity or value

e: Outturn for a month means work completed and transferred out of the workshop during the period, expressed in quantity or value, not wages or suspense balance.

q:
Consider the following statements about on-cost behaviour in a workshop:
1. As the volume of outturn of a workshop increases, the fixed on-cost per unit of outturn decreases.
2. The variable on-cost per unit of outturn remains broadly constant with changes in the volume of outturn.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are correct: fixed on-cost per unit falls as outturn volume rises, while variable on-cost per unit remains broadly constant with volume changes.

q: The cost accounts of a railway workshop are integrated with its financial (Government) accounts. The connecting link between the two sets of accounts is:

options.A: The Workshop Manufacturing Suspense head in the financial books and the Workshop General Register in the cost books
options.B: The Stores Ledger kept in the stores depot
options.C: The Contractor's Ledger of the workshop
options.D: The Traffic Book of the railway

e: Cost and financial accounts are linked through Workshop Manufacturing Suspense in the financial books and the Workshop General Register in the cost books.

q: Banaras Locomotive Works at Varanasi, a production unit manufacturing locomotives, was formerly known as:
e: Banaras Locomotive Works at Varanasi was formerly known as Diesel Locomotive Works before receiving its present name.

q: The workshop of South Eastern Railway which ranks among the largest railway workshops in India is situated at:
e: Kharagpur is the South Eastern Railway workshop which ranks among the largest railway workshops in India.

q: In the maintenance management of workshop machinery, the indicator 'MTBF' (Mean Time Between Failures) shows:

options.A: The average time taken to repair a machine after a breakdown
options.B: The total downtime of the workshop in a month
options.C: The average life of a machine before it is condemned
options.D: The average time for which a machine operates between successive failures

e: MTBF, Mean Time Between Failures, is the average time a machine operates between successive failures; average repair time is MTTR.

q: An outline process chart prepared in the method study of a workshop job is distinguished by the fact that it records:

options.A: Only the main activities of the process, namely the operations and inspections, omitting the subsidiary movements and delays
options.B: Every transportation, delay and storage in full detail
options.C: The wages payable for each operation of the job
options.D: The simultaneous movements of the two hands of the operator

e: An outline process chart records only the main activities, operations and inspections, omitting subsidiary transport, delays and storage.

q: A two-handed process chart prepared in the method study of a workshop operation records:

options.A: The work of a man and of the machine attended by him, side by side
options.B: The movements of the two hands of an operator, recorded against a common time scale
options.C: The pattern of movement of men and materials in a work area
options.D: The sequence of operations, inspections and delays in a process

e: A two-handed process chart records the movements of the two hands of an operator against a common time scale for method study.

q: Case hardening of a steel component in a workshop is distinguished from through hardening in that, in case hardening:

options.A: The whole section of the component is hardened uniformly throughout
options.B: The component is softened all over so that it can be machined easily
options.C: Only the outer surface (case) is hardened, the core remaining comparatively soft and tough
options.D: The component is given a protective coating of zinc

e: In case hardening only the outer surface or case is hardened and the core remains soft and tough, unlike through hardening of the whole section.

q: After a hole is drilled in a component, 'reaming' is carried out on it in a workshop in order to:

options.B: Cut internal threads in the hole
options.C: Make the hole oval in shape
options.D: Finish the hole to an accurate size and a smooth surface

e: Reaming finishes a drilled hole to an accurate size and smooth surface with a reamer; tapping cuts internal threads.

q: Case hardening, as a surface-hardening process in a workshop, is ordinarily applied to components made of:

options.A: Low-carbon (mild) steel, so that the surface hardens while the core remains tough

e: Case hardening is ordinarily applied to low-carbon or mild steel, so the surface can be hardened while the core remains tough.

q: A cylinder bore turned out in a workshop is to be finished to a fine surface finish and close limits by working it with abrasive stones. The finishing operation required for this purpose is:
e: Honing finishes a cylinder bore to a fine surface and close limits by working it with abrasive stones.

q: The lathe operation of 'knurling' performed on a component in a workshop consists of:

options.A: Cutting a helical groove on a cylindrical surface
options.B: Reducing the diameter of a workpiece by a forming tool
options.C: Producing a roughened (diamond or straight) pattern on a cylindrical surface so as to provide a better grip
options.D: Facing the end of a workpiece square to its axis

e: Knurling produces a roughened diamond or straight pattern on a cylindrical surface to provide a better grip.

q: A fitter in a workshop obtains a very fine surface finish and a close fit on a machined component by rubbing its surface with loose abrasive paste. This finishing process is known as:
e: Lapping gives a very fine finish and close fit by rubbing a surface with loose abrasive paste.

q: A fitter in a workshop has to cut an external screw thread on a bolt by hand. The hand tool he will use for this work is a:
e: An external screw thread on a bolt is cut by hand with a die; a tap cuts internal threads.

q: In a gear shaping machine in a workshop, the gear teeth are generated by means of:
e: In a gear shaping machine, gear teeth are generated by a reciprocating pinion-shaped cutter.

q: Timber received in the wood-working shop of a workshop is 'seasoned' before use in order to:

options.A: Reduce the moisture content of the timber so that it does not warp, shrink or crack in service
options.B: Harden the surface of the timber
options.C: Protect the timber against white ants
options.D: Give a smooth finish to the timber

e: Timber is seasoned to reduce its moisture content so it does not warp, shrink or crack in service.

q: For the batch production of small turned components, a turret (capstan) lathe is preferred to an ordinary centre lathe in a workshop because:

options.A: It can machine much longer workpieces than a centre lathe
options.B: It works at much higher spindle speeds than a centre lathe
options.C: A number of tools set in the turret can be brought into operation one after another in sequence, without re-setting for each operation
options.D: It does not require a skilled operator at all

e: A turret or capstan lathe suits batch production because several tools set in the turret can be used one after another in sequence without re-setting each time.

q: The surface of a steel component in a workshop is heated rapidly with an oxy-acetylene flame and is then immediately quenched. This surface-hardening treatment is known as:
e: Flame hardening rapidly heats a steel surface with an oxy-acetylene flame and immediately quenches it to harden the surface.

q: To enable the head of a bolt to sit below the surface, the upper portion of a drilled hole in a workshop is enlarged with a flat bottom. This machining operation is called:
e: Counterboring enlarges the upper portion of a drilled hole with a flat bottom so a bolt head can sit below the surface.

q: For marking out work and for carrying out inspection in the fitting section of a workshop, reliance is placed on an accurately flat reference surface provided by the:
e: A surface plate provides the accurately flat reference surface used for marking out work and for inspection in the fitting section.

q: Seam welding, employed in a workshop for making leak-proof joints such as in tanks and containers, consists of:

options.A: A continuous fillet weld made by an arc process
options.B: Joining by heating the parts in a furnace
options.C: A series of overlapping spot welds produced by roller (wheel) electrodes

e: Seam welding makes leak-proof joints by a series of overlapping spot welds produced by roller or wheel electrodes.

q: In a hardness test carried out on a workshop material, a square-based diamond pyramid is pressed into the specimen under a specified load and the impression is measured. The test being performed is the:
e: The Vickers hardness test presses a square-based diamond pyramid into the specimen under a specified load and measures the impression.

q: Surface and near-surface defects in an electrically conductive component of a workshop are to be detected without destroying the component, by a test based on currents induced in it. This non-destructive test is:

options.D: Ultrasonic testing of thick castings only

e: Eddy current testing induces currents in a conductive component to detect surface and near-surface defects without destroying it.

q: The lathe operation known as 'parting off' in a workshop means:

options.A: Cutting off the finished workpiece from the bar stock
options.B: Producing a flat surface at the end of a workpiece
options.D: Reducing the diameter of the workpiece over a part of its length

e: Parting off is cutting off the finished workpiece from the bar stock on a lathe.

q: Before painting, the castings and steel structures in a workshop are cleaned and descaled and rust is removed from their surface by impelling shots at high speed upon it. This surface-cleaning process is called:
e: Shot blasting cleans, descales and removes rust from castings and steel structures by impelling shots at high speed before painting.

q: The finest measurement that a micrometer screw gauge in ordinary workshop use can ordinarily record accurately is:
e: A micrometer screw gauge in ordinary workshop use can ordinarily record accurately to 0.01 mm, its usual least count.

q: A foundry mould which is dried or baked in an oven before the molten metal is poured into it, and which is generally preferred for large castings, is known as a:
e: A dry sand mould is dried or baked in an oven before pouring and is generally preferred for large castings; a green sand mould is used moist.

q: A machine component in a workshop fails after a long period of service under repeated fluctuating (cyclic) stresses, although the stress levels were well below the ultimate tensile strength of the material. Such a failure is classified as:
e: Fatigue failure occurs under repeated fluctuating stresses well below ultimate tensile strength after long service; creep is time-dependent deformation at high temperature.

q: The narrow gap or clearance between two mating parts, such as the clearance between mating surfaces, is measured most suitably in a workshop with:
e: Feeler gauges, thin blades of known thickness, most suitably measure a narrow gap or clearance between mating parts.

q: A smith in the smithy of a workshop shortens the length of a workpiece so that its cross-section increases. In forging terminology, this operation is known as:
e: Upsetting shortens the length of a workpiece so its cross-section increases; drawing out lengthens it and reduces cross-section.

q: The run-out (eccentricity) and alignment of a rotating component such as a wheel or a shaft in a workshop are checked primarily with a:
e: A dial gauge or dial test indicator checks run-out, eccentricity and alignment of rotating components such as wheels and shafts.

q: The external diameter of a cylindrical component such as a shaft turned in a workshop is checked with a gauge known as a:
e: A ring gauge checks the external diameter of a cylindrical component such as a shaft; a plug gauge checks internal diameters.

q: 'Simplification', as applied to the components and materials used in a workshop, consists mainly of:

options.A: Laying down the standard specifications to which a component must conform
options.B: Inspecting every component of a batch before it is accepted for use
options.C: Reducing the unnecessary variety of types and sizes of components to the minimum necessary
options.D: Giving a separate code number to every variety of component in use

e: Simplification reduces unnecessary variety of types and sizes of components and materials to the minimum necessary; specification is standardisation.

q: Before a drilled hole in a workpiece is enlarged to its final size, a small hole is drilled in advance to guide the larger drill which follows it. This preliminary hole is called a:
e: A pilot hole is a small hole drilled in advance to guide the larger drill that enlarges the hole to final size.

q: The 'machinability' of a metal, as the term is used in a machine shop of a workshop, refers to:

options.A: The ease with which the metal can be cast into the required shape
options.B: The ease with which the metal can be machined, judged by tool life, surface finish and the power required
options.C: The ease with which the metal can be welded to other metals
options.D: The resistance offered by the metal to corrosion in service

e: Machinability is the ease with which a metal can be machined, judged by tool life, surface finish and power required.

q: 'Grouting' carried out during the installation of a machine in a workshop consists of:

options.A: Filling the space under the base of the machine with cement grout so that it is secured truly and its load is distributed over the foundation
options.B: Applying a thick coat of paint to the foundation to protect it from oil
options.C: Packing the bearings of the machine with grease before it is started
options.D: Levelling the floor of the shop by laying a fresh layer of concrete over it

e: Grouting fills the space under a machine base with cement grout so it is secured truly and its load is distributed over the foundation.

q: The thickness of sheet metal and the diameter of wires in a workshop are checked by trying them in the graded slots of an instrument known as a:
e: A wire gauge checks sheet thickness and wire diameter by trying them in its graded slots.

q: While closing the monthly accounts, the Workshop Accounts Officer adds up the balances shown against individual jobs in the register that records work-order-wise expenditure and outturn. This aggregate is expected to tally with:

options.A: The balance under Stores Suspense in the general books
options.B: The balance of the shop on-cost account for the month
options.C: The balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense in the general books
options.D: The total of unpaid wages held by the workshop

e: The aggregate of work-order-wise balances in the Workshop General Register is expected to tally with the balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense in the general books.

q: In his periodical scrutiny of the work-order register of the workshop, the Workshop Accounts Officer is chiefly on the look-out for:

options.A: Jobs that have remained incomplete or outstanding for long periods, so that their early clearance can be secured
options.B: Errors in the rates of wages payable to shop staff
options.C: Items to be included in the annual Works Programme of the railway
options.D: Shortages in the cash balance held in the workshop imprest

e: In scrutiny of the work-order register, the Workshop Accounts Officer looks mainly for jobs incomplete or outstanding for long, so their early clearance can be secured.

q: The Workshop Accounts Office insists on receiving a copy of each work order at the time it is issued. The purpose served by this copy is that the Accounts Office can:

options.A: Purchase the material required for the job on behalf of the shop
options.B: Keep watch over the charges booked against that work order and build up the cost of the job in its register
options.C: Decide the wages of the staff who will be employed on the job
options.D: Arrange the sale of the finished articles of the job

e: A copy of each work order lets the Accounts Office watch charges booked against it and build up the job cost in its register.

q: A workshop unit and a divisional accounts unit periodically agree their Account Current with each other. The object of this agreement is to satisfy both units that:

options.A: The cash balances held by the two units are equal
options.B: All workers of the workshop have been correctly paid
options.C: The outturn programme fixed for the workshop has been achieved
options.D: Every debit and credit advised by one unit has been accepted and brought to account by the other, and outstanding differences are cleared

e: Agreement of Account Current satisfies both units that every debit and credit advised by one has been accepted and brought to account by the other, clearing outstanding differences.

q: A workshop settles the cost of work done for another accounting unit not in cash, but through its monthly Account Current. Settlements of this kind are known as:
e: Settlement of work done for another accounting unit through the monthly Account Current, and not in cash, is a transfer transaction.

q: Which of the following pairings about the two parts of the Workshop Outturn Statement is correct?

options.A: Part I – outlay on jobs; Part II – work completed by each shop
options.B: Part I – work done or completed by each shop; Part II – expenditure incurred on the jobs
options.C: Part I – on-cost percentages; Part II – balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.D: Part I – machines held by each shop; Part II – arrears of wages of shop staff

e: In the Workshop Outturn Statement, Part I shows work done or completed by each shop and Part II shows expenditure incurred on the jobs.

q: For compiling the monthly statement of outturn and outlay of the shops, the Workshop Accounts Office principally relies on:

options.A: The stores price ledger maintained in the stores depot
options.B: The cash book of the workshop cash office
options.C: The completion reports and the returns of outturn and expenditure rendered by the shops
options.D: The muster rolls of casual labour engaged in the shops

e: For the monthly outturn and outlay statement, the Accounts Office relies principally on completion reports and returns of outturn and expenditure rendered by the shops.

q: The charges accumulated against a job under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense are taken out of that suspense head:

options.A: In one lump sum at the end of the year, for all jobs taken together
options.B: Only when the Railway Board specifically orders the clearance
options.C: By transferring all the debits to shop on-cost at the end of every month
options.D: Separately for each job when it is completed, on the strength of its completion report and the outturn statement

e: Charges under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense are cleared separately for each job on completion, on the strength of its completion report and the outturn statement.

q: Which statement correctly brings out the field covered by the Machinery and Plant Programme?

options.A: It covers plant and machinery needed by workshops, sheds, depots and other units all over the railway, not by workshops alone
options.B: It is confined to plant and machinery for locomotive workshops only
options.C: It is confined to production units manufacturing locomotives
options.D: It covers only the plant and machinery of the Railway Board's office

e: The Machinery and Plant Programme covers plant and machinery needed by workshops, sheds, depots and other units all over the railway, not workshops alone.

q: A zonal railway wants a fresh item taken into the Rolling Stock Programme. The itemised proposal for this purpose is put up by the railway to:

options.A: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: A zonal railway puts up its itemised proposal for a fresh Rolling Stock Programme item to the Railway Board.

q: A clerk tracing the sanction of a work taken into the Rolling Stock Programme or the Machinery and Plant Programme for the year will find the itemised sanctioned works listed in the railway's:

options.B: Works Programme, popularly called the Pink Book

e: Itemised sanctioned works under the Rolling Stock and Machinery and Plant Programmes are listed in the railway's Works Programme, popularly called the Pink Book.

q: The programme to which a repair workshop mainly works is drawn up with reference to:

options.A: The production programme for new rolling stock of the railway
options.B: The Machinery and Plant Programme of the railway
options.C: A programme for manufacture of stores items only
options.D: The stock becoming due for Periodic Overhaul, that is, the overhaul arisings

e: A repair workshop mainly works to a programme drawn up with reference to stock becoming due for Periodic Overhaul, i.e. the overhaul arisings.

q: Finished articles handed over by a workshop to the stores depot are brought on to the stock of the depot at:

options.A: Cost of manufacture, made up of material, labour and on-cost
options.B: The prevailing market price of similar articles
options.D: A fixed rate notified for all workshops

e: Finished articles handed over to the stores depot are taken into depot stock at cost of manufacture, made up of material, labour and on-cost.

q: The cost sheet of a manufacture job is drawn up:

options.A: Before the work order is issued, as a rough forecast of cost
options.B: By the stores depot when the article is taken into stock
options.C: When the job is completed, from the charges that have accumulated under its work order
options.D: At the close of the year, for all jobs together in a single sheet

e: A manufacture job cost sheet is drawn up when the job is completed, from the charges accumulated under its work order.

q: Job cards, material requisitions and the completion report of a job all bear the number of its work order. This is done chiefly so that:

options.A: The stores depot can fix the issue price of material drawn for the job
options.B: Every item of labour, material and on-cost belonging to the job can be collected together under that work order
options.C: The pay of the workers employed on the job can be fixed
options.D: The job can be identified by the audit party during inspection

e: Job cards, material requisitions and the completion report all bear the work order number so every labour, material and on-cost item can be collected together under that job.
